# Risk strips and the Home cards

A risk strip sits at the top of Access Overview, Role paths, Who has access and Can they?: a few lines, worst first, each with a count and a link. A person or role gets one set of checks, an object another. Home shows the account's numbers from one pass over the findings.

## One line (`server.py:1731-1751`)
- `risk(bad, text, n, link)` -> `severity` `bad` | `warn` (`server.py:1731-1732`); `ranked()` puts `bad` first and keeps the built order within a tone (`server.py:1750-1751`).
- `more(xs)`: the first `RISK_TOP` (3) names, then `+N` (`server.py:1728`, `1735-1736`).
- `findings_risk(xs, to)`: the findings count per severity and the first 3 short rule names, worst severity first; `bad` when any is Critical or High (`server.py:1739-1747`).

## Person or role (`risks_of`, `server.py:1776-1811`; cached per subject by `subject_risks`, `server.py:1769-1773`)

| Line | When | Tone |
|---|---|---|
| Is admin role X | a role in `ADMIN` (its `ADMIN_POWER` text) | bad |
| Holds N admin roles: R via F | `admin_paths`, the shortest path per admin role | bad |
| N account privileges | `account_privs` not reached through PUBLIC | bad |
| Reads N sensitive objects unmasked | `seen_counts` (as the Access page counts) | bad |
| N rule findings (counts): names | findings whose grantee is the subject | bad if Critical / High |
| Default role is admin role X | user's `DEFAULT_ROLE` in `ADMIN` | bad |
| Disabled / Never logged in / Dormant, still holds N roles | `stale(name)` and roles held | warn |
| Very broad access | reads >= `BROAD` (25%) and >= `BROAD_MIN` (20) of the account's data objects | warn |
| Secondary roles ALL | `DEFAULT_SECONDARY_ROLES` holds ALL and more than one role held | warn |

- Constants: `server.py:1722-1728`; data object total `data_total()` (`server.py:1754-1755`).

## Object (`object_risks_of`, `server.py:1825-1856`; cached by `object_risks`, `server.py:1818-1822`)
- From the grants, without the Who has access walk, so Can they? stays fast: readers through `READ_PRIVS`, writers through `WRITES`, minus users lacking USAGE on its database or schema (`usage_gaps`) (`server.py:1826-1829`).
- Lines: sensitive columns without masking while someone can read it (bad); granted to PUBLIC (bad when sensitive); people, not service users, who can change a sensitive object (bad); disabled or dormant readers (bad when sensitive); rule findings naming the object; only admin roles reach it (warn); not used in `UNUSED` (90) days yet at least `WIDE` (3) users can read it, from `object_activity()` (warn) (`server.py:1832-1855`).

## Home (`home_page`, `server.py:1859-1872`)
- Shared view only for the risk numbers and cards; My access gets its own ladder counts (`server.py:1861-1867`).
- `home_summary()`, once per data set (`server.py:1875-1909`): findings per severity and per rule, distinct people and roles per severity, unmasked sensitive columns (rule 6, first `NAMES`), dormant readers (rule 7), governance KPIs. **Needs attention** (`act_first`): Critical, then High rules, rarest first so a rule with thousands of findings does not bury one with a few, at most `ACT_FIRST` (5), each with its first `NAMES` subjects (`server.py:1895-1899`, `1912`).
- `home_cards()`, once per data set (`server.py:1920-1968`): admin holders by admin role (service users apart, account privilege only counted), stale people by status, users by status and type, roles by kind, objects by type (`TOP_TYPES` 6 + Other), chain depth, biggest schemas and databases (`TOP_BIG` 6), daily queries of the last `DAYS` (60), object activity counts ([object-activity.md](object-activity.md)), and What changed counts only when that diff is already made: Home never compares (`server.py:1963-1968`).

## Tests
- `test_risks` (`test_server.py:1905`): the strip on Access Overview, Role paths, Who has access and Can they?.
